data.long_meaning: Derived from the English name 'Hattie', which is a diminutive of 'Hattie' meaning 'hat' and 'love'. In the Middle Ages, hats were symbols of protection, and the name was given to girls born under the sign of Venus, the Roman goddess of love. The name Hattie carries the meaning “Hat, love” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Hattie usually hope their child will grow to embody hat, love and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Hattie belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Hat, love.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hattie total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.
data.cultural_impact: The name Hattie holds a great cultural significance as it was popular among African Americans in the late 1800s and early 1900s in the United States. It was a name given to girls born into the slave community who were believed to have a strong spirit and a determination to overcome the hardships of their lives. Hattie CarVTte, a famous African-American actress, singer, and dancer, further popularized the name.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual realm, the name Hattie signifies resilience, determination, and strength. It is a name given to girls believed to possess a strong character and unwavering spirit. The name is also a reminder of the protective nature of God, who shields and cares for us like a hat shields us from the elements. Additionally, the name may carry significance as a reminder of Venus, the Roman goddess of love and beauty, representing the love and compassion that God has for all of his children.
